A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RoboMME study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices A–E support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on 16 simulation tasks, an 18-participant human study, and four real-robot tasks, with detailed results in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds OpenVLA-OFT evaluations, detailed MemoryVLA results, and analyses of memory contribution.

M1.justification: Appendix B.4 adds memory adaptations to OpenVLA-OFT's shared LLaMA architecture, including perceptual context using fused DINOv2/SigLIP features. This extends the implementation to another architecture while retaining the original 14 pi0.5-based designs and memory mechanisms.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 16 RoboMME simulation tasks, four real-world tasks, and human-study population. The additional models and analyses use existing task coverage; Appendix E's task requirements and configurations are unchanged.

E2.justification: v2 Table 15 adds OpenVLA-OFT without memory and four memory-augmented OpenVLA-OFT variants to the per-task comparison. Diffusion Policy and preliminary MemoryVLA evaluation already appeared in v1 Appendix C.4; MemoryVLA now receives full tabulated comparison. Main Table 3's comparator membership remains unchanged.

E3.justification: The reported recurrent batch size changes from 8 in v1 Table 7 to 16 in v2 Table 6, and recurrent inference changes from eight sampled frames to a buffer retaining up to 64 frames. v2 also introduces OpenVLA-OFT training protocols, a 1024-token memory condition, and a 160-episode attention analysis. These documented revisions do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v1 already studied memory budgets of 64–512 tokens in Figure 4. v2 Appendix C.5 extends this to 1024 tokens and adds attention-allocation and modulation scale/bias analyses, substantially expanding evidence about how memory influences action prediction.

E5.justification: The existing nine-run MME-VLA and three-run prior-method protocols are retained. However, v1 Table 12 identifies its summaries as mean and variance, whereas v2 Table 15 retains the ± notation without that definition. New Table 18 explicitly reports modulation means and standard deviations, describing activation variability rather than uncertainty in success rates.

E6.justification: Existing task-table values are retained, while v2 adds five OpenVLA-OFT result rows and MemoryVLA's per-task results. The latter average approximately 7.12%, replacing v1's preliminary 9% description without establishing identical settings. Appendix C.5 adds attention/modulation measurements and 1024-token success rates of 45.87% for FrameSamp+Modul and 40.17% for TokenDrop+Modul.

T1.justification: Appendix A retains the mathematical definitions, architectural equations, and flow-matching derivation. Correcting the language-token count symbol in A.1 is a notation correction, without changing the mathematical substance.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the benchmark contribution, four memory dimensions, 14 pi0.5 variants, task-dependent effectiveness, and favorable performance-efficiency balance of perceptual memory with modulation. Added appendix evidence does not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations for OpenVLA's weaker grounding and architectural integration constraints, plus interpretations involving sparse memory attention and modulation stability. It qualifies the single-backbone limitation with 'mainly' and removes v1's warning that MemoryVLA adaptation was unsuccessful. These changes extend the discussion while retaining its central conclusions.

D1.justification: Appendix B substantially expands reproducibility information: recurrent sampling, padding, masks, backpropagation and supervision details; model-specific hardware and training times; and complete OpenVLA-OFT, MemoryVLA, and Diffusion Policy configurations. It also adds explicit MME-VLA/OpenVLA code links and leaderboard access information. Much of this is newly disclosed detail, not demonstrated procedural change.

R1.justification: v2 adds references including OpenVLA, OpenVLA-OFT, Prismatic, and CogACT to support the expanded implementation discussion. The related-work taxonomy and principal novelty positioning remain unchanged. Numerous venue updates concern already-cited works rather than additional research.

P1.justification: Appendix B is reorganized by model, with MME-VLA settings and training configuration consolidated; Appendix C.4 is rewritten and C.5 added. Scattered wording corrections include replacing the erroneous real-robot 'TokenDrop+QwenVL' name with GroundSG+QwenVL, consistent with the unchanged Table 4. The main narrative remains largely intact.

P2.justification: The appendix gains three training-configuration tables and three memory-analysis tables. The complete results table gains comparator rows and moves onto a dedicated page, while existing training tables and prompt figures are relocated. This substantially expands the appendix's tabular presentation; the original figures and main-table designs are retained.

improvement.justification: The added backbone comparison and detailed training recipes make the benchmark more informative and reproducible, while Appendix C.5 supplies useful diagnostic evidence about memory use. These gains are tempered by recurrent-setting revisions left unreconciled with unchanged scores, removal of the MemoryVLA adaptation caveat without explicit validation, and less explicit uncertainty labeling in the full-results table.
